items.note: Introduces the Semantic Repulsion Technique (SRT) to reduce AI homogenization, with a computational evaluation and a 16-person user study comparing SRT with baseline AI systems on usefulness, coherence, and originality ratings; unclear whether participants wrote with each system or only rated system outputs, and N is far below 50.
Compares Alternate Uses Task responses from 256 humans with those of three AI chatbots; no participant receives AI help (an Author Correction exists, doi 10.1038/s41598-024-54745-y).

Controlled experiment with 148 participants brainstorming with an AI partner using a deepening versus a diversifying strategy (two AI configurations); stated outcomes are trust and adoption of AI ideas, so check the full text for any creativity or diversity score on the ideas.

Three groups of professional engineers and designers produce speculative-design ideas fully human, with AI as a tool, or fully by AI; experts rate 120 ideas for novelty, usefulness, and craft, and cosine similarity measures design-space breadth; group assignment and N not stated, likely small.

Within-group experiment in which 35 UX design students generate 214 concepts with and without ChatGPT, with expert creativity ratings plus self-reported creative confidence; order randomization not stated and N below 50.

385 participants write stories in an AI creativity-training program under four conditions (automated feedback or not, adaptive or constant difficulty), with pre and post Alternate Uses Task scores; check whether the feedback comes from generative AI and whether the comparison isolates AI assistance.

Two preregistered parallel randomized experiments (1,100 participants combined; per-experiment N not stated) compare a standard LLM, a coach-like LLM, and no AI on divergent and convergent thinking tasks, with a final unassisted stage (with_ai and after_ai); CHI 2025 version of arXiv 2410.03703.

Observational analysis of 2.1M preprints, 28K review reports, and 246M accesses finds LLM adopters write more papers and access and cite more diverse prior work; the only diversity outcome is citation diversity, not idea diversity, so it may be marginal for this section (arXiv 2601.13187 is the author version).

Longitudinal analysis of 81,663 college applications (2020 to 2024) with detector-estimated LLM use, reporting post-2023 convergence in surface-level linguistic features of admissions essays by SES and links to admission outcomes.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, and Springer page all failed); the title suggests an empirical study of ChatGPT and idea creativity on open innovation platforms, so the design (observational or experimental) needs checking in the full text.
